cases.prompt_restraint: Gives exact tower, eventual equality, universe and classification goals, without naming the dual colimit, tensor model, product test or finite-stage retract condition.
cases.rubric_fairness: A full invariant criterion with both directions, countable-limit relation and transformations is legitimately required; all equivalent concise proofs are accepted. Optional retract, finite-limit and examples are not mandatory.
cases.shortest_valid_completion: Identify F as M tensor -, enumerate countable torsion-free M in the countable Z-product comparison to force finite generation, dualize finite free M, and determine transformations from their Z components.
cases.static_difficulty: medium for the complete classification; concise expert proof remains valid; no empirical difficulty claim

checks.item: Finite-free dual tensor-Hom isomorphisms and transition compatibility; tensor-colimit identity is given by mutually inverse representative formulas.
The colimit is countable and torsion-free without injectivity of transitions.
Canonical countable product comparison detects finite generation by enumerating all elements; finite generation plus torsion-freeness gives finite free M and representing object M*.
Evaluation at Z and naturality along 1->a classify all group-valued transformations, with correct variance, identity and composition.
Optional finite-stage idempotent/retract criterion is proved in both directions; finite-limit preservation and projection/localization examples are valid.
Universe, zero-group, rank-zero and empty-diagram cases are within scope.

cases.prompt_restraint: No preselected quotient space or stabilizer criterion is supplied. Quotient universality, descent realization and arbitrary-base compatibility are linked primary goals rather than a proof recipe.
cases.rubric_fairness: Allows effective-topos descent and internal stabilizer formulations with verified hypotheses. Requires all tests and arbitrary bases because these are actual quantified claims. Boundary examples are optional.
cases.shortest_valid_completion: Construct the sheaf orbit relation, show the action factors through its effective kernel pair exactly when internal stabilizers act trivially, and apply effective descent; identify quotient and pullback as inverse functors and use base-change stability.
cases.static_difficulty: medium and framework-dependent; standard topos results allow a short proof; no calibrated long-answer claim

checks.item: Finite-cover local orbit relation gives a separated presheaf; matching-family gluing gives a sheaf, local surjectivity and exact local orbit equality.
The comparison E -> H fiber-product_Q E/Gamma is locally surjective without global representative choices.
Trivial stabilizer action on every test object is exactly the missing injectivity condition; constant-gamma tests extend to local group elements.
Quotient and pullback are mutually inverse on objects and all morphisms; uniqueness with chosen realization identifications is distinguished from automorphisms.
For arbitrary nonrepresentable B over Q, H_B/Gamma is B; base-change classification and coordinate-reordering compatibility are correct.
Dense integer orbit and point-invisible negation examples are valid and fully retain their stated hypotheses.
V-valued sheaves and all gluing constructions have legal size; empty tests, T and base are covered.

Its universal property can also shorten the all-parameter step once the natural probe representation is established.

kification and all-probe natural transformation identification are valid; products are identified only after kification.

Both directions of the k compact-open exponential law are complete; uncurrying restricts ordinary evaluation to the compact image of a probe and does not require local compactness of the whole source.

The Q-to-R ordinary compact-open evaluation counterexample has a valid compact avoidance and positive-denominator continuous function.
